First, we calculate the derivative of $r(t):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-2t+2)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t-1)\,j \\  & =(2t-2)\,i+\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $r(t)$ are parallel for some specific value ${t}_{0}$ of the parameter $t$ if and only if there exists a constant $c$ such that $r({t}_{0})=c\,{r}^{′}({t}_{0}).$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =c\,{r}^{′}(t) \\ ({t}^{2}-2t+2)\,i+(t-1)\,j & =c((2t-2)i+\,j) \\ ({t}^{2}-2t+2)\,i+(t-1)\,j & =c(2t-2)i+c\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients of $i$ and $j$ gives:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{t}^{2}-2t+2=c(2t-2) \\ t-1=c\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we obtain $t-1=c.$ Substituting $c=t-1$ into the first equality, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2}-2t+2 & =(t-1)(2t-2) \\ {t}^{2}-2t+2 & =2{t}^{2}-4t+2 \\ {t}^{2}-2t & =0 \\ t(t-2) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $r$ and ${r}^{′}$ are parallel at the points corresponding to $t=0$ and $t=2.$

Finally, since

$$
\begin{aligned}r(0) & =({0}^{2}-2(0)+2)\,i+(0-1)\,j=2\,i-\,j, \\ r(2) & =({2}^{2}-2(2)+2)\,i+(2-1)\,j=2\,i+\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

we conclude that $r(t)$ and ${r}^{′}(t)$ are parallel at the points $(2,-1)$ and $(2,1).$
